blocks.content: I packed my pencils into the side pocket of my bag and closed the sketchbook. The drawing was still there, obviously. I wasn't going to tear it out. I'm not dramatic. I was just going to close the book and not think about it.
Mr. Alvarez appeared at my elbow with his rag, though there was nothing near me that needed cleaning.
You're leaving early.
Told you. Going to paint from life.
Outside.
That's where life usually is.
He nodded at my bag.
What are you bringing?
Travel easel. Some oils.
I hesitated.
The sketchbook.
He made that sound again.
My clouds look like mashed potatoes. I know. You told me.
They did. Very emotionally supportive mashed potatoes.
I always laugh at that. Which is exactly why he keeps saying it.
I stood, picked up my bag. The morning had filled in while I sat — more people on the street now, the town properly awake, the light gone from gold to the regular kind.
Ethan.
I turned. He was looking at the window.
Sometimes a painting finds you before you find it.
I looked at the window. Then back at him.
I have no idea what that means.
I know. Take your coffee.
I took my coffee. I left.
